newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds were cheered by strength in German bond markets and a slightly firmer tone in the U.S. Treasury market in the afternoon.

The Swiss March Confederate bond futures contract, which expires March 17, ended firm but below highs. The benchmark 4-1/2 percent 10-year government cash bond was also higher, once again yielding below 3.50 percent.

"Volume was smaller than in recent days. Today there was no real sales pressure," one Swiss-based trader said, adding there was some follow-up buying in the long end. "But it is still too early to talk about a change in trend," the trader added.
With respect to new foreign bond offerings, syndicate managers for Credit Suisse First Boston said an issue led by the firm for J.P. Morgan went well.
J.P. Morgan launched a 200 million Swiss franc issue this morning, which matures in October 2005, and was priced at 102.65 with a coupon of 3.50 percent.

"A good borrower. Tight but right," said one syndicate manager of the deal. He said there were 26 banks in the syndicate, some with large committements. He said the issue was offered late on Monday at 3.47 percent.
March Comi medium-term bond up nine at 112.24
Mar Euro Swiss francs up two at 98.12.
